# Ambient clock (`ambient-clock`)

A screensaver for wall and bedside screens: large clock, date, next event and weather, dimmed at night.

Group: Home controls. Styles: `import '@mosaic-home/design-system/css/home';` (or `style.css`).

## Web API

`createAmbientClock` (types in `dist/web/home/info/ambientClock.d.ts`): `.mh-ambient-clock` (`.is-night`): a screensaver face, centred. `__face` holds a `time.__time` (`__digits` and a smaller `__period` in 12-hour time) and a `__date`; under them `__extras` with the `__event` (`__event-icon`, `__event-title`, `__event-when`) and the `__weather` (`__weather-icon`, `__temperature`, `__condition`). The face drifts by up to a large space step (`--_dx`, `--_dy`) and holds still under reduced motion. Not a live region: a ticking clock would talk all the time.

```ts
export function createAmbientClock(options: AmbientClockOptions): AmbientClockHandle;

export interface AmbientClockOptions extends InfoClockFormat {
  /** A fixed time to show. Without one the clock shows the current time and keeps itself up to date. */
  time?: InfoTime;
  /** Show seconds (default false; never at night). */
  seconds?: boolean;
  /** Show the date line (default true). */
  date?: boolean;
  nextEvent?: AmbientClockEvent | null;
  weather?: AmbientClockWeather | null;
  /** The dim look for a dark bedroom: low contrast, no accent, thin figures. */
  night?: boolean;
  /** Moves the content a few pixels now and then so nothing burns into the screen (default true; off when the user asks for reduced motion). */
  drift?: boolean;
  /** Time between drift steps, in ms (default 60 000). */
  driftEvery?: number;
  /** Accessible name (default "Clock"). */
  label?: string;
}

export interface AmbientClockHandle {
  el: HTMLDivElement;
  /** Applies changed options; omitted ones keep their value. */
  update(changes: Partial<AmbientClockOptions>): void;
  /** Stops the timers. */
  destroy(): void;
}
```

## Web example

```ts
import { createAmbientClock } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/web';

const atNight = (): boolean => {
  const hour = new Date().getHours();
  return hour >= 22 || hour < 7;
};

// Without a `time`, the clock keeps its own.
const clock = createAmbientClock({
  night: atNight(),
  nextEvent: { title: 'Bins out', when: '19:30' },
  weather: { condition: 'partly-cloudy', temperature: 14 },
});

setInterval(() => clock.update({ night: atNight() }), 60_000);

document.body.append(clock.el);
```

## React API

`AmbientClock` (types in `dist/react/home-info.d.ts`): Same DOM and classes as `createAmbientClock`; keeps its own time when `time` is absent.

```ts
export function AmbientClock({
  time,
  locale,
  hour12,
  timeZone,
  seconds,
  date = true,
  nextEvent,
  weather,
  night,
  drift = true,

  label = 'Clock',
```

## React example

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { AmbientClock } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/react';

const atNight = (): boolean => {
  const hour = new Date().getHours();
  return hour >= 22 || hour < 7;
};

export function AmbientClockExample() {
  const [night, setNight] = useState(atNight);

  useEffect(() => {
    const check = setInterval(() => setNight(atNight()), 60_000);
    return () => clearInterval(check);
  }, []);

  // Without a `time`, the clock keeps its own.
  return (
    <AmbientClock
      night={night}
      nextEvent={{ title: 'Bins out', when: '19:30' }}
      weather={{ condition: 'partly-cloudy', temperature: 14 }}
    />
  );
}
```
